proof-narrative-lean-equiv.evidence: Re-read at 7e202a6abc2. The definition block's lean.ref is fred2005:Fred2005.SkewedPoissonStructure, i.e. def:skewed-poisson-structure's declaration. Nothing in Lean formalises Def 1.11; the sibling .lean is comment-only. The lean-ref-owns-decl script check fails on the shared ref. A definition block needs its own declaration (or an honest placeholder), not another block's.

NEW reason (the shared-ref failure is resolved). Re-read at d44c45e6066. lean.ref Fred2005.StrongMult.IsStronglyMultiplicative resolves (lean-ref-owns-decl passes, 1 claimant) and compiles sorry-free (propext, Quot.sound). But it is not Def. 1.11. The Lean `smOp` takes `.` to be the product of A (`LinearMap.mul' R A`), i.e. the product of T, and its docstring says this is 'as in the paper'. It is not: Def. 1.11 (library sec-000 lines 397-406) defines `.` as the multiplication of S = (x)_i A_i, 'the map induced on T_X by X x X -> S_X (ordered embedding) T_X', i.e. the ORDERED product, and the block .md says exactly this ('the multiplication of S ... transported to T through a choice of ordering'). On generators x in X_j, y in X_i with j > i the two differ (y'x' versus the sorted x'.y'), and Prop. 1.13's proof uses y'x' = x'.y' + pi(y',x') precisely because `.` is the ordered product. So IsStronglyMultiplicative is a different condition from the one the block defines. The Remark 1.12 lemmas (prim_of_isStronglyMultiplicative, strongMult_prim_iff) are unaffected, since at primitives only products with 1 occur. Also stale: the sibling strong-multiplicativity.lean still says the condition is not formalised and that the ref names Fred2005.SkewedPoissonStructure.

da-lean-narrative-divergence.evidence: Re-read at d44c45e6066. lean.ref Fred2005.StrongMult.IsStronglyMultiplicative resolves (lean-ref-owns-decl passes, 1 claimant) and compiles sorry-free (propext, Quot.sound). But it is not Def. 1.11. The Lean `smOp` takes `.` to be the product of A (`LinearMap.mul' R A`), i.e. the product of T, and its docstring says this is 'as in the paper'. It is not: Def. 1.11 (library sec-000 lines 397-406) defines `.` as the multiplication of S = (x)_i A_i, 'the map induced on T_X by X x X -> S_X (ordered embedding) T_X', i.e. the ORDERED product, and the block .md says exactly this ('the multiplication of S ... transported to T through a choice of ordering'). On generators x in X_j, y in X_i with j > i the two differ (y'x' versus the sorted x'.y'), and Prop. 1.13's proof uses y'x' = x'.y' + pi(y',x') precisely because `.` is the ordered product. So IsStronglyMultiplicative is a different condition from the one the block defines. The Remark 1.12 lemmas (prim_of_isStronglyMultiplicative, strongMult_prim_iff) are unaffected, since at primitives only products with 1 occur. Also stale: the sibling strong-multiplicativity.lean still says the condition is not formalised and that the ref names Fred2005.SkewedPoissonStructure.
